title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-08-29
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: SBD > MR > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording captures a blazing early Working Man's era set with smoking Casey Jones, a monster New Orleans → Searchin' → Good Lovin' medley, and plenty of Pigpen‑fuelled magic.
ai_review.review: The show is a high‑energy snapshot of the Dead’s 1969 Working Man’s transition period, highlighted by a scorching Casey Jones, an early Easy Wind with heavy organ, and a super‑special New Orleans into Searchin' into Good Lovin' sequence. Reviewers rave about the pristine stereo soundboard mix that sounds both clean and deliciously “dirty,” making this a must‑listen for fans of Pigpen’s powerhouse performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (mostly 4–5 stars) and enthusiastic comments about both the performance and the stereo soundboard mix indicate an outstanding show with excellent recording quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo mix described as crisp, perfect and well‑balanced; reviewers note a “good and dirty” vintage sound that remains clear despite the tape’s age.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth, high‑energy flow with a highlight medley of New Orleans → Searchin' → Good Lovin'; Pigpen‑heavy numbers are well‑placed and keep the momentum roaring.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Leads vocals on Good Lovin', shines on guitar during Easy Wind, and delivers strong vocal presence throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass (and the drummers) lock in tightly, “killing” the groove especially on Good Lovin' and other pig‑filled numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Heavy organ (likely Tom Constanten) is prominent on Easy Wind, adding a dirty vintage texture to the early Working Man sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Tight, powerful drumming noted throughout; especially praised for driving rhythm on Good Lovin' and the high‑energy pig songs.
